expected_comments.body: Item.Get() runs once per BOM line inside the loop (N+1 database round-trips); read the required item data in bulk instead of per iteration.
CalcFields() runs inside the FindSet loop, issuing an extra query per row; calculate outside the loop or read the value directly instead of via the FlowField.
User.Get() runs in OnAfterGetRecord, which fires per rendered row, so scrolling triggers an N+1 lookup per line; cache or bulk-resolve the user names.
UpdateBOMLineWithCost runs even when Item.Get fails. Only write a cost after establishing that the Item buffer contains the requested item; otherwise report or preserve the missing-item state.
The persistent PurchRcptLine buffer is queried with IsEmpty and immediately FindSet using unchanged filters. Remove the redundant existence query.

description: True positive performance findings: loop_optimization (trimmed to 5 representative findings)

expected_comments.body: String concatenation with += inside a FindSet loop building CSV output. Each += allocates a new string, resulting in O(n²) performance for large record sets. — Use TextBuilder to accumulate the output string. TextBuilder.Append() is O(1) amortized and avoids repeated memory allocation.

String concatenation with += inside a repeat..until loop building the vendor report body text. Each concatenation copies the entire accumulated string, degrading performance as the string grows. — Use TextBuilder to construct the HTML body. Replace HtmlBody += with TextBuilder.Append() calls for efficient string building in loops.

CalcFields("Remaining Amount") inside the Vendor Ledger Entry loop issues one FlowField query per row. Call VendorLedgerEntry.SetAutoCalcFields("Remaining Amount") before FindSet() so the FlowField is calculated as rows are retrieved.
The CSV header and concatenated data records lack row terminators. Exporting multiple records combines header and data into a single malformed CSV row.

description: True positive performance findings: textbuilder (2 findings). String concatenation with += inside loops causes O(n²) memory allocations; TextBuilder should be used instead.

expected_comments.body: HttpClient.Post sends customer data (email, name, phone, address) to external CRM service without PrivacyNotice.GetPrivacyNoticeApprovalState() check in the code path — Add Privacy Notice consent verification before sending customer data externally

HttpClient.Post sends email data via Microsoft Graph API without PrivacyNotice.GetPrivacyNoticeApprovalState() check for Exchange integration consent — Verify Privacy Notice consent for Exchange/Graph integration before sending emails

Customer strings are interpolated directly inside JSON quotes. Quotes, backslashes or line breaks in customer data produce invalid or altered JSON. Serialize with JsonObject/JsonValue rather than manual interpolation.
Email subject, recipient and HTML are interpolated into JSON without escaping. Ordinary quoted HTML attributes can corrupt the request. Use structural JSON serialization.

HttpClient.Post's Boolean result is captured, but only the true branch is handled. A false transport result silently leaves the item Pending without failure/retry handling. Handle the false branch explicitly; this is not the omitted-Boolean case, which raises on transport failure.

The remote send can be accepted before the transactional Sent status commits. If the transaction rolls back, the next Pending scan can send the same email again. Establish explicit retry/reconciliation semantics for this non-atomic boundary; an arbitrary identifier in a Graph request is not evidence of provider-side deduplication.
This user-facing Error, Message or Confirm call uses a Text literal rather than a Label (AA0216). Move the message template into a label.
